name: UniD3
description: UniD3 includes a multiple KG and drug–disease datasets from PubMed biomedical literature. Use over 150,000 PubMed articles, contain high-quality information for drug–disease matching, drug effectiveness assessment, and drug–target analysis.

name: RepoDB
description: A standard drug repurposing database linking approved and failed drugs to diseases based on clinical trial outcomes. Widely used as a benchmark for computational drug repurposing.

name: FAERS
description: FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) collects spontaneous reports of adverse events and medication errors submitted by healthcare professionals, consumers, and manufacturers.

name: TRANSCRIPT DRUG REPURPOSING DATASET
description: A dataset for drug repurposing using transcriptomic signatures, combining gene expression data from drug treatments and disease states to identify repurposing candidates.

name: DRUGMECHDB
description: DrugMechDB is a database of curated drug mechanism-of-action paths representing the biological mechanism by which a drug induces its primary indicated effect in a disease.

name: openFDA Human Drug
aim: FDA drug data API/downloads across events, labels, approvals, and more
source: FDA Drug Event, Drug Label (SPL), NDC, Drugs@FDA, Drug Shortages, Drug Enforcement
description: openFDA provides structured APIs and bulk downloads for FDA human drug data across six endpoints: Drug Adverse Events, Drug Labeling (SPL), National Drug Code Directory, Drugs@FDA approvals, Drug Shortages, and Drug Enforcement (recalls).

name: DailyMed
description: DailyMed is the official U.S. provider of FDA label information (package inserts) for prescription and OTC drugs, offering full-text structured product labeling (SPL) documents.

name: DrugBank
description: DrugBank is a comprehensive, freely accessible, online database containing detailed drug data with drug-target interaction information. It integrates chemical, pharmacological, and pharmaceutical data with drug targets, transporters, enzymes, and carriers.

name: RxNorm
description: RxNorm provides normalized names for clinical drugs and links to drug vocabularies used in pharmacy management and drug interaction software. Maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

name: DrugEHRQA
aim: QA on drug information in EHR
source: MIMIC-III, n2c2 (ADE and Medication Extraction Challenge)
description: A question-answering dataset on structured and unstructured EHR data focused on drug-related queries. Supports evaluating NLP models on clinical drug information extraction.

name: WebMD Drug Reviews
aim: Patient-reported drug effectiveness and side effects
description: A dataset of patient drug reviews from WebMD, including drug name, condition treated, effectiveness rating, ease of use, and side effect descriptions. Useful for NLP and pharmacovigilance research.

name: ChEMBL
description: ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties, containing binding, functional, and ADMET data for small molecules tested against drug targets.

name: Open Targets Platform
source: Integrated from GWAS, literature, clinical trials, omics
description: The Open Targets Platform integrates genetic, genomic, and chemical data to systematically identify and prioritize drug targets for human diseases, providing evidence scores for target-disease associations.

name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
aim: Expert-curated pharmacological receptor and drug data
description: The IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY is an expert-curated, open access, drug discovery database providing expert-curated pharmacological data on drug targets and the substances that act on them.

name: SIDER
description: SIDER (Side Effect Resource) contains information on marketed medicines and their recorded adverse drug reactions, mined from public documents and package inserts.

name: nSIDES
aim: Adverse event reports mining for drug effects/interactions
source: FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS); EHR for validation
description: nSIDES provides OFFSIDES (single-drug side effects) and TWOSIDES (drug-drug interaction side effects) resources derived from FAERS adverse event reports using statistical signal correction methods; complementary analyses validated against electronic medical records.

name: DGIdb
description: DGIdb (Drug-Gene Interaction Database) mines existing resources to curate drug-gene interaction data and gene druggability information, supporting drug repurposing and target identification.

name: TTD
source: Literature curation, FDA, WHO, clinical data
description: The Therapeutic Target Database (TTD) provides information about the known and explored therapeutic protein and nucleic acid targets, the targeted disease, pathway information, and the corresponding drugs directed at each of these targets.

name: DrugCentral
description: DrugCentral integrates structure, bioactivity, regulatory, pharmacological, and disease data for drugs approved for human or veterinary use, supporting drug repurposing and pharmacological research.

name: MecDDI
description: MecDDI provides mechanistic explanations for drug-drug interactions, annotating the biological mechanisms (e.g., transporter, metabolic enzyme, receptor) underlying each interaction.

name: DDInter
description: DDInter (v2.0) is a drug interaction resource covering 2,310 drugs with 302,516 drug-drug interactions (plus drug-food, drug-disease interactions, and therapeutic duplications), annotated with 8,398 distinct mechanism descriptions and clinical management recommendations.

name: DrugMAP
aim: Drug molecular atlas and multi-omics profiles
description: DrugMAP provides molecular atlas profiles including transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics data for drugs, enabling mechanistic understanding of drug actions.

name: DrugCombDB
description: DrugCombDB is a comprehensive database of drug combinations, collecting experimental synergy data from multiple sources including NCI-ALMANAC and literature for cancer therapy.

name: CDCDB
description: CDCDB (Continuous Drug Combination Database) is a continuously updated drug combination database covering 40,795 combinations (17,107 unique, spanning 4,129 individual drugs), curated from ClinicalTrials.gov, the FDA Orange Book, and patents. Designed to keep drug combination computational models up-to-date.

name: VigiAccess
description: VigiAccess provides public, aggregated access to the WHO VigiBase global pharmacovigilance database. Users can search by active ingredient to see counts of reported potential side effects grouped by active ingredient and continental region (individual case reports are not viewable due to data protection).

name: OREGANO
description: OREGANO is a biomedical knowledge graph designed for computational drug repurposing, distinguished by its integration of natural compounds alongside drug, disease, gene, and pathway data, enabling graph-based drug candidate identification via link prediction.

name: DRKG
aim: Drug repurposing knowledge graph for COVID-19 and beyond
source: Integrated from DrugBank, Hetionet, GNBR, STRING, IntAct, DGIdb
description: DRKG (Drug Repurposing Knowledge Graph) is a comprehensive biomedical KG built for drug repurposing, especially for COVID-19. It integrates data from six major databases covering drugs, genes, diseases, pathways, and compounds.

name: BindingDB
description: BindingDB is a public, web-accessible database of measured binding affinities, focusing on the interactions of proteins considered to be drug-targets and small, drug-like molecules.

name: ATC/DDD
description: The WHO ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical) Classification System classifies drugs into groups at five hierarchical levels based on organ/system acted on and chemical, pharmacological, and therapeutic properties.

name: UniTox
description: UniTox uses GPT-4o to process FDA drug labels and extract toxicity summaries and ratings across eight organ-system toxicities (cardio, liver, renal, pulmonary, hematological, dermatological, oto, infertility), with clinician validation showing 85–96% concordance.

name: Drug Repurposing Hub
description: The Drug Repurposing Hub is a curated and annotated collection of FDA-approved drugs and clinical candidates for use in repurposing screens, maintained by the Broad Institute's CLUE platform.

name: DDI Corpus 2013
description: The DDI Corpus 2013 is a benchmark dataset for drug-drug interaction extraction from biomedical text, containing manually annotated interactions from DrugBank and MEDLINE abstracts, used in the DDIExtraction 2013 SemEval task.

name: DrugProt
description: DrugProt is a BioCreative VII track dataset for relation extraction between drugs/chemicals and gene/proteins in biomedical literature, covering 13 relation types.

name: ADE Corpus
description: The ADE Corpus v2 contains annotated medical case reports for adverse drug event detection and drug-dose entity extraction, widely used for NLP benchmarking in pharmacovigilance.

name: n2c2 2018 Track 2
aim: Drug and adverse event extraction from clinical notes
description: The n2c2 2018 Track 2 dataset provides annotated clinical discharge summaries for extraction of adverse drug events and medication entities including drug name, dosage, frequency, route, and ADE.

name: CADEC
description: CADEC (CSIRO Adverse Drug Event Corpus) is annotated with adverse drug event mentions extracted from patient forum posts, enabling NLP research on consumer health text and informal drug reporting.

name: askapatient
description: AskaPatient.com is a website where patients report their experiences with prescription medications, including ratings for effectiveness, side effects, and ease of use.

name: PsyTAR
description: PsyTAR (Psychiatric Treatment Adverse Reaction corpus) contains annotated user reviews for psychiatric medications, labeled with adverse drug reactions, drug indications, and withdrawal symptoms.

name: TAC 2017 ADR
aim: Adverse drug reaction extraction from drug labels
description: The TAC 2017 Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) task provides FDA drug labels annotated with adverse reactions, including reaction mentions, MedDRA normalization, and severity levels, for biomedical NLP benchmarking.

name: PHEE
description: The PHEE dataset includes 5,000+ richly annotated pharmacovigilance events from public medical case reports. It covers two event types (adverse and potential therapeutic), and annotates each event’s trigger plus hierarchical arguments: main spans (subject, treatment, effect) and fine-grained sub-arguments such as subject demographics/conditions and treatment details (drug, dosage, frequency, route, timing, duration, target disorder).

name: Drugs.com
description: Drugs.com provides a comprehensive consumer drug information database with drug descriptions, side effects, interactions, dosage guidelines, and patient reviews.

name: Drug Reviews (Druglib.com)
description: A dataset of patient drug reviews from Druglib.com scraped for NLP research, containing drug name, condition, rating, and text review. Available via UCI ML Repository for sentiment and effectiveness analysis.

name: TarKG
description: TarKG is a comprehensive biomedical knowledge graph focused on target discovery, integrating multi-source data including traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) knowledge, with 171 relation types centered around disease, gene, and compound entities.

name: DrugRepoBank
description: DrugRepoBank collects and curates drug repurposing candidates and evidence from experimental, computational, and clinical sources to support systematic drug repositioning research.

name: RepurposeDrugs
description: RepurposeDrugs.org is a curated portal documenting drug repurposing opportunities, cataloging existing drugs being investigated for new indications with supporting evidence from trials and literature.

name: ReframeDB
aim: Repurposing compound library for infectious diseases
description: ReFRAME (Repurposing, Focused Rescue, and Accelerated Medchem) is a drug repurposing library of ~12,000 compounds assembled by Calibr, specifically intended for anti-infective and neglected disease repurposing screens.

name: DrugRepurposing Online
description: DrugRepurposing Online is an open-access, crowdsourced gold-standard drug repurposing database (by Numedicus) focused on experimentally validated content: 479 indications, 1,031 mechanisms, 4,326 repurposing opportunities with 4,862 literature references, recently integrated with the Guide to Pharmacology.

name: NCATS Pharmaceutical Collection (NPC)
aim: Approved drug compound library for screening
description: The NCATS Pharmaceutical Collection is a library of ~3,300 drugs (72% approved, 28% investigational) assembled from FDA, EMA, and Japanese PMDA sources, curated for drug repurposing screens.

name: LINCS L1000
description: LINCS L1000 contains gene expression signatures from 978 landmark genes measured after perturbation with drugs, genetic knockdowns, and overexpression in multiple cell lines, enabling drug mechanism studies.

name: Clue
aim: Drug gene expression signatures for repurposing
description: The Clue links drug treatments to gene expression signatures, enabling discovery of functional connections among diseases, genetic perturbations, and drug candidates through shared transcriptional responses.

name: STITCH
description: STITCH (Search Tool for Interactions of Chemicals) integrates chemical-protein interaction data from experiments, databases, and text mining, covering both direct (binding) and indirect (functional) interactions.

name: SuperDRUG2
description: SuperDRUG2 is a comprehensive database of approved drugs with 3D structures, pharmacokinetic data, side effects, and targets, supporting structure-based drug design and ADMET modeling.

name: PROMISCUOUS 2.0
description: PROMISCUOUS 2.0 integrates drug-protein interactions and protein-protein interaction networks to analyze drug polypharmacology and off-target effects, supporting multi-target drug design.

name: e-Drug3D
description: e-Drug3D is a database of 3D structures for ~1,500 FDA-approved drugs (1,300+ unique compounds, MW <2000), based on the Drugs@FDA Data File, enabling analysis of drug scaffolds, pharmacophores, and chemical diversity of the approved drug space.

name: ZINC
aim: Commercially available compound library for virtual screening
description: ZINC is a free database of commercially available compounds for virtual screening, providing 3D structures for docking and pharmacophore-based drug discovery with annotations for drug-likeness and biological activity.

name: Open TG-GATEs
source: In vitro/in vivo toxicology studies (pharmaceutical consortium)
description: Open TG-GATEs (Toxicogenomics Project-Genomics Assisted Toxicity Evaluation System) provides gene expression and pathology data for ~170 compounds in rat liver and primary human hepatocytes under various doses and time points.

name: DrugMatrix
source: NTP (National Toxicology Program) in vivo studies
description: DrugMatrix is the world's largest toxicogenomic reference database, containing gene expression data from rat studies for hundreds of drugs and chemicals under well-defined conditions, supporting mechanism-of-toxicity analysis.

name: ToxCast
description: ToxCast (Toxicity Forecaster) is an EPA program providing high-throughput screening data for thousands of chemicals across hundreds of in vitro assays to prioritize chemicals for further toxicological testing.

name: LiverTox
source: NIH/NLM literature synthesis and clinical data
description: LiverTox is an NLM/NIH resource providing detailed, referenced information on the diagnosis, cause, frequency, patterns, and management of liver injury attributed to prescription and non-prescription drugs.

name: TOXRIC
aim: Comprehensive toxicity data for ML benchmarking
source: Aggregated from ChEMBL, PubChem, ToxCast, eToxPred
description: TOXRIC is a comprehensive toxicity database covering 1,474 toxicity endpoints across 13 toxicity categories for 113,372 compounds, providing standardized benchmark splits for machine learning toxicity prediction models.

name: SynergyFinder
aim: Drug combination synergy analysis and data
description: SynergyFinder is a web application and database for interactive analysis and visualization of drug combination synergy/antagonism data, offering multiple synergy scoring models (Loewe, Bliss, ZIP, HSA).

name: DrugComb
aim: Drug combination response data for cancer
description: DrugComb is an open-access data portal for drug combination response data in cancer cell lines, integrating data from multiple large-scale screens with harmonized synergy scores across multiple models.

name: DCDB (Drug Combination DB)
description: DCDB (Drug Combination Database) provides information on approved and investigational drug combinations, including combination rationale, component drugs, targets, and relevant diseases.

name: MoleculeNet
description: MoleculeNet is a benchmark suite for molecular machine learning, consolidating datasets for molecular property prediction including quantum mechanics, physical chemistry, biophysics, and physiology (ADMET) tasks.

name: TDC (Therapeutics Data Commons)
aim: Unified ML benchmarks for drug development
description: TDC (Therapeutics Data Commons) is an open platform providing machine-learning-ready datasets, benchmarks, and data functions for therapeutics and drug development tasks including ADMET, DTI, DDI, and drug combination prediction.

name: IDG
description: Integrates human protein, bioactivity, and drug target development level data to support drug discovery.

name: KIBA
source: ChEMBL kinase activity data (Ki, Kd, IC50 unified)
description: KIBA (Kinase Inhibitor BioActivity) integrates multiple kinase inhibitor bioactivity metrics (Ki, Kd, IC50) into a unified KIBA score, serving as a benchmark for drug-target affinity prediction.

name: NDF-RT (National Drug File)
aim: Drug classification by mechanism and physiologic effect
source: VA National Drug File, NCI Thesaurus
description: NDF-RT (National Drug File-Reference Terminology) is an ontology of drug mechanisms of action, physiological effects, and chemical structures that extends the VA National Drug File drug terminology.

name: CancerDR
description: CancerDR is a database providing pharmacological profiles of anticancer drugs against cancer cell lines, along with information on drug targets, resistance mechanisms, and cell line characteristics.

name: PRISM DepMap
description: The PRISM (Profiling Relative Inhibition Simultaneously in Mixtures) DepMap dataset provides large-scale drug sensitivity data across cancer cell lines from the DepMap project, enabling identification of biomarkers of drug response.

name: GDKD (Genomics-Drug Knowledge DB)
aim: Genomic markers of drug response in cancer
description: GDKD integrates genomic features (mutations, CNV, methylation) with drug response data across multiple cancer cell line pharmacogenomics datasets to identify genomic determinants of drug sensitivity.

name: ALMANAC
description: NCI ALMANAC (A Large Matrix of Anti-Neoplastic Agent Combinations) provides systematic cancer drug combination screening data for ~5,000 pairs of approved anticancer drugs tested on the NCI-60 cell line panel.

name: PharmKG
aim: Pharmacology KG benchmark for link prediction
source: Integrated from OMIM, DrugBank, PharmGKB, TTD, SIDER, HumanNet, GNBR
description: PharmKG is a multi-relational, attributed biomedical knowledge graph benchmark for the pharmaceutical domain integrating gene-disease, chemical-gene, chemical-disease, and chemical-chemical relationships for link prediction tasks.

name: RxList Drug Descriptions
description: RxList provides comprehensive, FDA-approved drug monographs including indications, contraindications, side effects, mechanism of action, pharmacology, and clinical pharmacology for healthcare professionals.

name: MedlinePlus Drug Info
source: NLM / AHFS Drug Information (American Society of Health-System Pharmacists)
description: MedlinePlus Drug Information provides plain-language, consumer-friendly information about drugs and supplements including usage, side effects, precautions, and storage, maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

name: WHO Essential Medicines List
aim: Global essential drug list for primary healthcare
source: WHO Expert Committee on Selection and Use of Essential Medicines
description: The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (EML) represents the minimum medicine needs for a basic health-care system, listing drugs by therapeutic category with dosage forms and strength specifications.

name: DrugSig
source: GEO microarray data, DrugBank, KEGG, CTD, TTD
description: DrugSig is a database of drug-induced transcriptomic signatures curated from public repositories, enabling drug repurposing by connecting drug signatures to disease signatures.

name: EK-DRD
description: EK-DRD (Experimental Knowledge-based Drug Repositioning Database) provides drug repositioning annotations for 1,861 FDA-approved and 102 withdrawn small-molecule drugs, integrating 30,944 target assay records, 3,999 cell assay records, 585 organism assay records, and 8,889 clinical trial records linked to ~1,799 targets, 856 diseases, and 1,332 pathways.

name: DrugOOD
description: DrugOOD is a systematic OOD (out-of-distribution) benchmark suite for drug discovery, providing multiple dataset splits based on scaffold, size, and drug type to evaluate generalization of molecular ML models.

name: M3-20M
description: M3-20M is a large-scale multi-modal molecular dataset containing 20 million molecules with SMILES, molecular graphs, and natural language descriptions, designed for pre-training molecular foundation models.

name: Polaris
source: Aggregated from industrial and academic partners
description: Polaris is a benchmark platform for drug discovery providing high-quality, rigorously designed benchmark challenges submitted by industry and academic partners, addressing issues of data leakage and realistic evaluation.

name: GDSC/GDSC2
description: The GDSC (Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer) database contains pharmacological profiles for ~500 drugs tested in ~1,000 cancer cell lines with matched genomic data, enabling biomarker discovery for drug response.

name: CTRP (Cancer Therapeutics Response Portal)
description: CTRP provides drug sensitivity data (AUC, EC50) for ~481 small molecules across ~860 cancer cell lines with matched molecular data (mutations, expression), supporting identification of predictive biomarkers.

name: GEO Drug Perturbation Signatures
description: GEO Drug Perturbation Signatures aggregates drug-induced gene expression data from NCBI GEO, providing a comprehensive collection of transcriptomic responses to drug treatments across cell lines and tissues.

name: DILIrank 2.0
aim: Curate and model drug safety data from ChEMBL
source: Drug Safety Data Curation and Modeling in ChEMBL, Chemical Research in Toxicolog
description: Reviews systematic curation of drug safety data (e.g., boxed warnings and withdrawn drugs) from the ChEMBL bioactivity database and discusses methods to model these safety outcomes for toxicology and drug discovery research.

name: ADReCS
aim: Adverse drug reaction ontology and classification
description: ADReCS (Adverse Drug Reaction Classification System) provides a hierarchical classification of adverse drug reactions and integrates ADR information across multiple data sources with standardized MedDRA terminology.

name: DTC (Drug Target Commons) 2.0
description: Drug Target Commons (DTC) is a community platform for drug-target interaction data, providing curated and standardized bioactivity data aggregated from multiple public databases with target annotations.

name: PubChem
aim: Chemical compound database and bioassay data
description: PubChem is the world's largest publicly accessible chemical database maintained by NCBI, providing information on the biological activities of small molecules including chemical structures, properties, patents, and bioassay results.

name: ChEBI
description: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) is a freely available dictionary of molecular entities with ontological classifications, focusing on small chemical compounds relevant to biology.

name: FDA Orange Book
source: FDA Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
description: The FDA Orange Book (Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations) lists all FDA-approved drugs with patent and exclusivity information, therapeutic equivalence ratings, and approval details.

name: HMDB (Human Metabolome Database)
aim: Human metabolite and drug metabolite data
description: HMDB is a comprehensive database of small molecule metabolites found in the human body, including drug metabolites, with chemical, clinical, and molecular biology data for each metabolite.

name: SemaTyP
aim: discover candidate drugs and drug–disease associations
description: A structured knowledge graph linking drugs, diseases, and biomedical entities (genes, proteins, pathways) extracted from literature. Each edge represents a potential interaction or association, with semantic types inferred from co-occurrence and ontology mappings. This dataset is intended for downstream drug discovery tasks, including candidate drug identification, repositioning, and hypothesis generation.

name: Tahoe
description: Tahoe-100M is one of the largest public single-cell drug perturbation datasets, profiling ~1,200 drugs across cancer cell lines at single-cell resolution, supporting mechanistic drug studies and foundation model pre-training.

name: DRMref
description: DRMref is a curated database of drug resistance mechanisms built from single-cell RNA-seq data (42 datasets spanning 13 cancer types, 35 treatments, 42 drugs, and 1.6M+ cells), providing analyses of cellular composition, EMT, cell-cell interactions, and pathway enrichment for resistance characterization.

name: PharmacoDB
source: GDSC, CCLE, CTRP, NCI-60, gCSI, PRISM, FIMM
description: PharmacoDB integrates large-scale cancer pharmacogenomics datasets (GDSC, CCLE, CTRP, PRISM, etc.) with standardized annotations, enabling cross-study comparison of drug sensitivity and biomarker discovery.

name: CPIC
source: Expert curation, FDA PGx labeling, literature
description: CPIC (Clinical Pharmacogenomics Implementation Consortium) provides peer-reviewed, regularly updated pharmacogenomics prescribing guidelines to help clinicians interpret genetic test results and optimize drug therapy.

name: SYNERGxDB
source: Integrated from NCI-ALMANAC, MERCK, DECREASE, CLOUD, and other drug combination studies
description: SYNERGxDB is a web portal for exploring, analyzing, and visualizing drug combination synergy data from multiple pharmacogenomics studies, providing standardized synergy scores and biomarker analysis tools.

name: KEGG Drug
aim: Approved drugs and their molecular mechanisms
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes
description: A curated database containing chemical structures, drug targets, metabolic pathways, and drug–drug interactions, integrated with KEGG pathway and disease maps to support pharmacological research and drug discovery.

name: Molecular Targets Platform
description: The Molecular Targets Platform is powered by a GraphQL API that supports graphical queries for a single entity or target-disease association across our knowledge graph. Please note that our API is optimised for a single query.

name: NLM-Chem-BC7
aim: Chemical entity recognition and indexing in biomedical full-text
source: PMC full-text articles, NLM indexer annotations
description: NLM-Chem-BC7 comprises two complementary BioCreative VII Track 2 resources: an Identification corpus of 204 full-text PMC articles with ~61,000 chemical mention annotations normalized to MeSH identifiers, and an Indexing corpus of 1,333 full-text articles manually indexed with chemical subject headings by NLM indexers. Designed for chemical NER, entity linking, and indexing prediction in biomedical NLP.

name: JUMP-Cell Painting
aim: Morphological profiling of chemical and genetic perturbations (Cell Painting)
description: Largest public Cell Painting morphological-profiling dataset: image-derived features for ~116,000 chemical and genetic perturbations across billions of cells; used for MoA prediction, repurposing, and toxicity.

name: Cell Painting Gallery
aim: Open repository hosting Cell Painting image-based profiling datasets
description: AWS Open Data repository aggregating JUMP and other Cell Painting datasets (raw images + extracted morphological features) for image-based profiling.

name: RxRx3
aim: Image-based phenomics map of genetic and chemical perturbations
description: Phenomics dataset of ~2.2 million images spanning ~17,000 genetic and ~1,600 compound perturbations; image-based morphological profiling.
